label: Claude Sonnet 5.5

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: Morning, everyone. Thanks for joining. Rachel, Tom, this is Priya Natarajan, our sales engineer. Priya, over to you.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: Thanks, Marcus. Tom, Rachel mentioned you'd rather skip the slides, so I'd love to start with your questions.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: Good, my first question is what this has to touch. If it needs a hole in the firewall, we're going to have a long conversation. We've had vendors promise nothing touches our network and then ask for a VPN two weeks in.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: It doesn't touch your network at all. Each truck gets a gateway on cellular. The warehouse gateway uses cellular, too. And nothing on your side has to open a port.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: Low K.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: So the dock Wi-Fi never comes into it, because the dock Wi-Fi is, let's say, a work in progress. Half the time the handhelds drop off it in the freezer.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: Never, if a truck loses signal, the gateway stores the readings and sends them when it reconnects.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: What about logins? I'm not managing another set of passwords. We already have six vendors with their own portals, and every time someone leaves, I'm the one chasing those accounts down.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: We support single sign-on, so your people use the accounts they already have, and you turn someone off in one place.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: And the data, who owns it, where does it live, and how long do you keep it? Those three answers decide a lot for me.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: You own it. It's stored in the United States. We keep two years of history by default, and you can export all of it whenever you want.

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: Two years matters to us. Some customers ask for a full year of records, and I'd rather not be at the edge.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: Okay, then my other question is the routing software. Does this talk to it or is it?

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: It does. We send a nightly file, or we push each delivery's readings to the stop record through an API.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: The nightly file is fine to start. I'd rather not open up the routing system to anyone until we've lived with this for a while.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: Rachel, last week you said the alerts have to reach the right person fast. What does fast mean for you?

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: Five minutes. Overnight we've only got one dispatcher, so if a unit drifts at two in the morning, dispatch should know within five minutes, and if nobody acknowledges it, it comes to me.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: That's how escalation works. Dispatch and the driver get the first text, and if nobody acknowledges it in five minutes, it goes to the next person on the list.

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: And the driver app has to work with no signal. Half our routes go through dead zones out past the county line, and the drivers can't sit around waiting for a bar of service.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: It does. The app keeps logging and syncs later.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: Can I ask how a decision like this gets made at Rhyolite? Who else weighs in besides the two of you?

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: I make the recommendation. Tom has to sign off on security, and nothing gets past him without that. And anything over $25,000 goes to Linda Marsh, our CFO, for approval.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: And the board.

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: No, it doesn't go that far. Linda's the final word.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: Got it, and is Brinewatch the only option you're looking at?

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: We're also talking to Frostgauge. Their hardware came in about 30% cheaper, but they don't have a driver app, and that's a big deal for us.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: That's helpful to know. So before any of this goes to Linda, what would you need to see?

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: A pilot, a few trucks on real routes, ideally the ones with the worst dead zones, and alerts that actually show up at 2 in the morning.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: We could do four trucks for 30 days, installed at your yard overnight, so no truck comes off the road.

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: That works. Installs at night matter because we can't pull trucks during the week. We're running every truck we have right now.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: I'll need your security questionnaire filled out before anything gets installed. I can send hours over by Friday. It's long, so give yourselves some time.

segments.speaker: SE
segments.text: Perfect, and I'll send you a written pilot plan for the four trucks by Thursday.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: And Rachel, would you be up for bringing Linda to a call next week, once she's seen the plan?

segments.speaker: OPS
segments.text: Yes, next Tuesday at 10 again. I'll bring Linda.

segments.speaker: AE
segments.text: Great, I'll send the invite. Thanks, both of you. This was really useful.

segments.speaker: IT
segments.text: Thanks.

reply: {"strengths": [{"text": "Marcus handed off to the SE with a clean introduction and then let the technical questions run, which kept the call focused on what the buyers cared about.", "segment": "d2-s001", "quote": "Priya, over to you."}, {"text": "He turned a vague need into a concrete number by asking what 'fast' means, and Rachel answered with a five-minute alert window and escalation to her.", "segment": "d2-s016", "quote": "What does fast mean for you?"}, {"text": "He asked how the decision gets made and uncovered that Tom signs off on security and the CFO, Linda Marsh, approves anything over $25,000.", "segment": "d2-s021", "quote": "Who else weighs in besides the two of you?"}], "improvements": [{"text": "When Rachel named the competitor Frostgauge and said their hardware is about 30% cheaper, Marcus said 'That's helpful' and moved on without asking how price compares with the missing driver app or what matters most to Linda.", "segment": "d2-s028", "quote": "That's helpful to know."}, {"text": "The board question was a short leading prompt that Rachel quickly shut down, so a more open question about what Linda looks for when approving spend would have told him more about the final decision.", "segment": "d2-s023", "quote": "And the board."}, {"text": "Marcus asked for the next meeting with Linda but never confirmed what Tom's security questionnaire timeline means for the pilot start, even though Tom warned it is long and must be done before any install.", "segment": "d2-s034", "quote": "would you be up for bringing Linda to a call next week"}]}
